page.layout: One printed page. A single column of running text fills the page. Below the last line, at centre-left, is the gathering signature "Q 4". The running head is at the top, with the page number at top right. Two faint marks at the right margin near the foot (n, u, n) are show-through from the reverse and are left out.

main_text.l: funt. 1. Ut eodem eminentiæ gradu utrumque re-
gimen Deo subfit: Politicum vero subordinatur Deo
instar Dominatus, ecclesiasticum est tantum famu-
litium, & simplex ministeriū inferius subjectum : uti
loquitur Rollocus Edenburgenæ ecclesiæ pastor &
professor ὁμολογείμς[?] in 1. Thessal. 5. 12. 13. 2. ut
parem[?] potestatem vice versa in se invicem habeant:
ecclesiastica potestas rebus ad politicam potestatem
pertinentibus se non immiscet, & si officio suo desit,
non potest contra eam, nisi via monitionis procede-
re, docet solum, suadet, monet, rogat. At potestas
politica Christiani magistratus se extendit ad exter-
num ecclesiæ regimen quoad indifferentia & muta-
bilia, & si deviet potestas ecclesiastica, coactiva vi
instruitur. 3. Ut æquali potentia populum sibi con-
creditum moderentur : potestas ecclesiastica verbo
aberrantes oves arcet, & recolligit, persuadendo
servit hominibus qui Christo se submiserunt: Po-
litica vero ubi facinorosos legibus subjectos tenue-
rit, magnam quam obtinet, declarat potestatem,
& invitos cogit recedere à perversis suis moribus,
cogendo dominatur. Atque hæc ad rationem secun-
dam, qua ostenditur Episcopatum inter mutabilia
disciplinæ non fuisse agnitam ab ecclesia Scotica,
neque disciplinam omnem mutabilem esse, nec pro
arbitrio principis supremi policiti in essentialibus
mutari posse, aut ad idæam politici regiminis con-
formari. Si cui duriora hæc videbuntur, ac calum-
niis imminutæ majestatis regum arcessat, quasi hu-
jus sententiæ fautores desertis hic reformatis in Ie-
suitarum castra transfugerent ; (prout non puduit
maledicum rabulam inter plaustra illa convitiorum
& nequissimarum calumniarum, quibus afflictam
ecclesiam Scoticâ frustra onerare satagit, in putido
isto famoso libello, quem obstetricantibus furiis non
ita pridem extrusit, sub titulo fictitiæ epistolæ con-gratu-

page.notes: The Greek word after "Rollocus ... professor" (ὁμολογείμς) is uncertain and marked [?]. "parem" is uncertain: the word on the scan looks like "pafem", with long s. "instar" is read from "initar", with some doubt. The page has no marginal notes. Show-through at the right margin (n, u, n) is omitted. The text runs on from the previous page and continues to the next one ("gratu-"), so it is one paragraph. The running head "IN REGNO SCOTIA." is as printed.
